neighbours.label: foundation metaphors: the slot where a text calls something the backbone / cornerstone / mainstay / lifeline / staple of something else (fires on ' the' before it and on the metaphor's first piece); output promotes 'cornerstone', 'backbone', 'foundation', 'pillar'
fire: For decades, fishing was the backbone of the coastal villages.
Many doctors say that sleep is a cornerstone of good mental health.
In winter the ferry is the lifeline of the small island community.
Steroid injections remain the mainstay of treatment for this condition.
Volunteers have always been the backbone of the local fire brigade.
Trust between partners is the cornerstone of any lasting marriage.
Beans and corn were the staple diet of the farmers in the valley.
The railway became the lifeline of the mining towns in the north.
quiet: For decades, fishing brought work to the coastal villages.
Many doctors say that sleep can help with mental health problems.
In winter the ferry runs twice a day to the small island.
Steroid injections are sometimes given for this condition.
Volunteers often join the local fire brigade in the spring.
Trust between partners can grow slowly over the years.
Beans and corn grew in the fields of the farmers in the valley.
The railway reached the mining towns in the north in 1890.
